newsitem.title: CROATIA: RBA wants to buy into Croatian Franck.
newsitem.headline: RBA wants to buy into Croatian Franck.

text.p: The Croatian subsidiary of Raiffeisenbank Austria (RBA) said on Monday it wanted to buy into Croatia's leading coffee and snacks manufacturer Franck.
"We have no intention to take over the firm, but believe it is a good investment," RBA official Marko Delic told Reuters.
The bank is interested in buying Franck shares for its own portfolio, he said.
It is currently running a series of advertisements in Croatian newspapers offering a per share price of 540 kuna to Franck's current shareholders.
"For now the interest is quite strong," Delic said, but declined to provide any figures for the size of the proposed purchase.
There was no immediate reaction from the company to RBA's move. Franck has an equity of 42.7 million German marks, split into shares with a face value of 100 marks each.
Small private investors, mostly current and former employees, are estimated to control over 60 percent in it.
But Frank's shares are not freely traded on Zagreb's bourse or an over-the-counter market in Varazin.

The state privatisation agency has no holding left after it made a reservation of 27.55 percent for pre-World War Two owners. It also swapped a 8.14 percent stake with creditors for Franck's debt and disbursed some shares to war invalids. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
